review.tagline: LLM tracing, evals, datasets and prompt playground built on OpenTelemetry
review.summary: Phoenix collects traces from LLM applications through OpenTelemetry/OpenInference instrumentation and shows them in a web UI. It also covers LLM-based evals, versioned datasets, experiments, prompt management and a prompt playground that can replay traced calls. It runs via pip, uvx, Docker or a Helm chart, and exposes a remote MCP endpoint at /mcp for coding agents.
review.audience: Teams debugging and evaluating LLM apps who want self-hosted tracing
strengths: Install with pip or uvx and run `phoenix serve`; no separate setup shown
Auto-instrumentation for LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, DSPy, Vercel AI SDK and more
Built-in MCP server at /mcp lets Claude Code and Cursor query traces
Python and TypeScript packages for OTel, client and evals
weaknesses: License reported as NOASSERTION; terms need checking before commercial use
Managed production workflows are pushed to the paid Arize AX product
Azure template serves plain HTTP and needs a TLS proxy in front
RAM, storage backend and default port not stated in the README excerpt
needs: Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google GenAI, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter
